provenance.original: To estimate how many new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to be appointed each year, TSA first estimates the number of existing coordinators and alternates.  TSA accomplishes this by multiplying the number of Owner/Operators for each mode by 2 which results in 898 coordinators for freight rail (449 × 2), 484 for passenger rail (242 × 2), and 144 for OTRB (72 × 2).  TSA uses the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) turnover rates to estimate that approximately 4 percent of the current population of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate Cybersecurity Coordinators will separate from their positions and require replacement each year.  In addition, TSA estimates that approximately 9 percent of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to submit updated contact information each year.  This results in approximately 13percent of Owner/Operators having to submit new or updated Cybersecurity Coordinator designations in a given year (4% due to turnover + 9% due to updated contact information).  Applying this percentage to the population of covered Owner/Operators results in 117 new Cybersecurity Coordinators per year for freight rail operators (898 Owner/Operators × 13%), 63 for passenger rail (484 Owner/Operators × 13%), and 19 for OTRB (144 Owner/Operators × 13%).  Table 2 presents the annual hour cost burden associated with the designation of new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternates due to employee turnover.

provenance.original: Based on past estimates, TSA estimates that it will receive approximately 9,000 claims on an annual basis, or 750 per month.  Currently, all claims are submitted manually.  TSA estimates that it will take 30 minutes to complete and submit the forms, which results in an estimated burden of 4,500 hours.  Additionally, TSA collects payment information from those members of the public whose claims are approved by TSA.  TSA estimates that approximately 1,250 claims are approved each year.  TSA estimates it takes ten minutes (0.1667 hours) to submit payment information for an annual hour burden of 208 hours.  TSA estimates the public average annual hour burden of 4,708 hours (4,500 + 208).  To estimate annual hour burden cost, TSA multiples each hour burden by a fully-loaded wage rate of $38.91.  TSA estimates an annual hour burden cost of $175,095 for filing a claim and $8,106 for submitting payment information, for a total annual hour burden cost of this collection of $183,201.  Therefore, the total 3-year hour burden cost of this collection is $549,604 ($183,201 x 3 = $549,604).

provenance.original: TSA has moved away from using a TSA contracted medical provider to conduct the TSO candidates’ medical exam.  As such, the federal cost burden has changed.  The government cost no longer includes $2,531,250 in annual fees paid to a contracted medical provider.  However, TSO candidates will now incur an out-of-pocket cost to use a local health care provider to conduct a medical exam and complete the new Medical Clearance Form.  TSA estimates the cost burden to TSO candidates for medical exams at approximately $2,700,000 (18,000 exams x $150 per exam).  Since TSA staff will now be responsible for processing the SOMQ and Medical Clearance Form, cost estimates have been updated to account for the time required by an I-band employee to conduct the necessary review of these medical forms.

provenance.original: The TSA TWIC program is funded entirely by applicant fees and is not augmented by appropriated funding (see Question 13).  The TWIC fee covers applicant enrollment, vetting, adjudication, redress procedures and credentialing, and other operational costs associated with the program based on population estimates.  As the TWIC is a 5-year credential, the TWIC revenue model must ensure that the program remains viable for the lifetime of the credential.  In consideration of the TWIC program’s revenue model, TSA’s annualized cost for the Information Collection Request is $78.7 million (see Table 18).  The forecast provides the basis for estimating program costs to include enrollment services, security threat assessment, maintenance and modernization of backend IT systems, and credential maintenance services.

provenance.original: According to Office of Management and Budget’s Circular A-4, transfer payments are monetary payments from one group to another that do not affect total resources available to society.  To the extent that fee revenue for TWIC enrollments is in excess of the Federal costs of administering the TWIC program, the difference between costs and revenue would be transfer payments.  For more information, visit: https://www.whitehouse.gov/sites/whitehouse.gov/files/omb/circulars/A4/a-4.pdf

provenance.original: OTRB Owner/operators: TSA estimates that the 70 OTRB current owner/operators will conduct security training for each employee once every 3 years, and their records will be updated after each training.  TSA estimates an average of 3,663 current employees will be trained each year.  In addition, TSA estimates an average of 3,900 new training records due to turnover, and that 36 new OTRB owner/operators will create training records for their existing employees each year.  TSA estimates each new OTRB respondent has 157 employees who require security training, or a total of 36 x 157 = 5,652 responses.  TSA estimates that each response would have a time burden of 1 minute (0.01667 hours).  TSA estimates the average annual cost by multiplying the average annual time burden by the average industry compensation rate for an OTRB Administrative Assistant ($25.60).  The average annual cost of OTRB owner/operators recordkeeping is depicted in Table 8.
